questions.q: What is the exact fix this lesson applies to dbo.usp_CustomerOrderHistory's bottleneck?
options: A new covering nonclustered index on Orders keyed on (CustomerID, OrderDate DESC) with OrderStatus, OrderTotal, and ShipDate as INCLUDE columns
Rebuilding the clustered index on Orders
Adding a NOLOCK hint to the SELECT statement
Increasing MAXDOP for the instance
questions.explain: The new index's key covers the seek and sort, and its INCLUDE columns cover every remaining SELECT column, eliminating the Key Lookup entirely.

questions.q: Why is OrderDate DESC placed in the index's key rather than only in INCLUDE?
options: So the index is already sorted the way the query's ORDER BY needs it, avoiding a separate Sort operator
INCLUDE columns cannot store date data types
It has no effect either way on the plan
It is required syntax for every nonclustered index
questions.explain: Matching the key's column order to the query's ORDER BY lets the engine read rows already in the needed order instead of sorting afterward.

questions.q: What does this lesson do with the old IX_Orders_CustomerID index, and why?
options: Drops it, because it's now redundant and would otherwise tax every write with no remaining benefit
Leaves it in place permanently as a backup in case the new index fails
Rebuilds it with a higher fill factor
Converts it into a filtered index
questions.explain: Per Chapter 3's index-tuning workflow, a superseded index should be dropped — keeping both means paying maintenance cost twice for no added benefit.

questions.q: Which of these does this lesson explicitly NOT do, to keep the change deliberate and targeted?
options: Change MAXDOP, rebuild unrelated indexes, or add a NOLOCK hint to mask the symptom
Create any new index at all
Reference the diagnosis from Lesson 48
Use real T-SQL syntax
questions.explain: The lesson makes exactly one change — the one Lesson 48's diagnosis called for — rather than a shotgun mix of unrelated tweaks.

questions.q: Why does making one deliberate, targeted change (rather than several at once) matter for Lesson 50?
options: It lets Lesson 50 verify a clean before/after comparison with exactly one variable changed
It has no bearing on how validation works
It guarantees the fix cannot possibly fail
It removes the need to measure anything afterward
questions.explain: Chapter 1's loop depends on isolating one change so that a later measurement can attribute any improvement (or regression) to that specific change.
